newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank expects to beat cost save target.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank expects to beat cost save target.

text.p: NationsBank Corp chairman Andrew Craig said Wednesday the company expects to exceed the previously announced target of $175 million in 1997 cost savings from its merger with Boatmen's Bancshares but he declined to give a figure.
"We expect to exceed that," Craig said at a news conference following the annual meeting of shareholders. "I don't have that figure at hand immediately."

Chief executive Huge McColl told the meeting that system conversion in the merger is due to be completed by the fourth quarter of 1997. He said expenses from the system changes "are running well under what had been planned."

Craig, who headed Boatmen's before the merger, said the company will launch an advertising and marketing campaign in mid-June in the St. Louis area which would address concerns about the impact of the merger.
He said the company would try to win back investment management business that it lost following the merger.
Boatmen's, with $41.2 billion in assets, was the largest St. Louis-based bank up until the merger with Charlotte, N.C.based NationsBank. NationsBank was more than four times as big based on assets.
"Sure, we've lost some business, but in terms of our total operations it is not a substantial amount," Craig said.
